subject: Renewal: volume-easing rebate schedule and short-term price hold
messages:
From: Kai Huang <kai.huang@arcadia-analytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@arcadia-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — spike in usage and smoothing options

Vanessa,

Quick note as we kick off renewal planning for Q1: we expect a ~30% YoY bump in inference volume due to a new recommendation pipeline going live in January. We love the latency/price tradeoffs with Redwood, but the step change creates budgeting headaches for our finance team.

Two asks up front: can we explore (1) a short-term price hold for the first 90 days post-renewal while we stabilize usage, and (2) a rebate structure or credits that smooth the effective rate if we hit the higher volumes? We have some internal guidance that any concession above 12% needs exec visibility.

Would appreciate a quick proposal — happy to jump on a call next week.

Thanks,
Kai Huang
Head of Platform
Arcadia Analytics

---
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Kai Huang <kai.huang@arcadia-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@arcadia-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — spike in usage and smoothing options

Hi Kai — thanks for the heads-up and congrats on the pipeline launch.

High-level we can do a combination of a short-term price hold and a volume-linked rebate. I attached a spreadsheet (proposed-rebate-schedule-v2.xlsx) that sketches two options:
- Option A: 90-day price hold at current rates + tiered retroactive rebate applied when cumulative monthly committed volume is exceeded (effective rebate 6–10% depending on tier).
- Option B: No upfront hold but an accelerated committed-tier discount (bigger rebate, 10–14%) with a 12-month amortized credit.

I pulled in a few folks internally for quick alignment. Can you tell me roughly how you expect spend to ramp across Jan–Mar? That will steer which option gives you better net economics. If either looks promising, I’ll route a final amendment for Legal and Finance review.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Monday to walk through the spreadsheet and lock the mechanics. Available 9–11am PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: proposed-rebate-schedule-v2.xlsx
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Arcadia renewal — pricing approach (need quick approval)

Team — forwarding the Arcadia thread. They’re forecasting ~30% uplift Jan–Mar and want a smoothing approach. My recommended framework below (I’ve attached a draft amendment):

Proposal summary (for internal review):
- 90-day price hold at current hosted rates (no change to per-token list rates) to give their engineers breathing room when the new pipeline ships.
- Volume-easing rebate: retroactive rebate once monthly commit thresholds are exceeded, paid as a credit applied to subsequent invoices. Tiers at 100%, 125%, and 150% of prior annualized usage.
- One-time enrollment credit for unused burst (up to $25k) if they commit to a 12-month renewal at the mid-tier.

Requested approvals / risks:
- Finance: can we approve up to a 12% net-effective concession for year 1 without escalating? Ben, quick ARR impact calc would be great.
- Product: Karthik, need confirmation that auto-burst behavior and KV-cache re-use assumptions are fine for measuring committed volume (we’ll define measurement as billable token consumption).
- Legal: I’ve flagged a short amendment with fall-through language — see amendment-draft-redlines.pdf. If Legal needs stronger audit/logging language, we may have to limit the retro rebate.

I’ll wait for a green-light today; Arcadia wants to finalize commercial terms by Wed so we can land the DocuSign envelope before year-end.

Thanks — V

Attachment: amendment-draft-redlines.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Arcadia renewal — pricing approach (need quick approval)

Vanessa — ran a quick sensitivity on the two options. Notes:
- Option A (90-day hold + retro rebate): worst-case net-effective concession if Arcadia maxes to 150% would be about 12.5% year 1. That is borderline but manageable if we structure the rebate as a bill credit (not a cash refund) and cap the total credit exposure to $200k.
- Option B (accelerated commit): better predictability; projected net-effective concession ~10% with tighter caps.

Recommendation: approve Option A with the following guardrails: 1) cap total rebate exposure to $200k, 2) define measurement as billed token consumption (UTC-aligned calendar months), 3) amortize one-time enrollment credit over 6 months.

If Legal signs off on the measurement language, I’m comfortable green-lighting without exec escalation. Mark-in for finance review: if they push for >12% concession we loop in Maria (VP Sales Ops).

—Ben
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Arcadia renewal — pricing approach (need quick approval)

Couple of product/measurement points to confirm before Legal finalizes:
1) Commit measurement: we should use billable token consumption (generation + prompt tokens) per UTC calendar month; this avoids per-request sampling variance.
2) Auto-burst: allow spikes but apply rolling 30-day smoothing window for commit determination to avoid brief traffic spikes gaming the tier.
3) KV-cache and prefix caching: we need to exclude server-side cached tokens from billed consumption (they’re not billable) — Laura, can you confirm our billing telemetry can separate those?

If those are feasible, product is good with Option A and the 90-day hold. I also suggest adding an auto-fallback clause: if sustained growth persists beyond Q1, we transition them to the mid-tier rates automatically and give a one-time reconciliation credit. Keeps ops overhead low.

—Karthik
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Subject: Agreed commercial framework and next steps

Kai / Priya — thanks again for the quick sync. Per our conversation, below is the commercial framework we’ll put in the amendment: 

1) 90-day price hold: list hosted rates will remain unchanged for Jan–Mar 2027.
2) Volume-easing retro rebate: tiers at 100%, 125%, 150% of Arcadia’s prior annualized usage. Retroactive rebates applied as invoice credits after monthly reconciliation (cap $200k). Measurement: billed token consumption (generation + prompt tokens), UTC calendar months; 30-day smoothing window for spikes.
3) One-time enrollment credit: $25k credit for unused burst, amortized over 6 months.

Next steps:
- I’ll send the redlined amendment to Priya and include the measurement language Karthik proposed.
- Legal/Finance have pre-approved under the internal guardrails (cap $200k, 90-day hold).
- DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e — expecting signature by Wed EOD.
- Attachments: proposed-rebate-schedule-v2.xlsx, amendment-draft-redlines.pdf, usage-runbook.pdf

If anything changes on your end (ramp numbers or timing), let me know — otherwise we’ll push the amendment this afternoon.

Best,
